q: How do I calculate the carbon footprint of a pair of socks?
title: Socks carbon footprint per pair
short: Weigh the yarn in a pair, including knitting waste, and multiply by your spinner's per-kg figure. Add knitting, toe linking, dyeing or washing, boarding with steam, labels and packing, then divide the unit's energy by pairs passed.
audience: Hosiery and sock makers, including Tiruppur and Ludhiana units

ul: Cotton, polyester, nylon and elastane by weight per pair.
Ask the spinner for a per-kg yarn figure; blends differ.
Circular sock knitting machines and toe linking.
Dyeing or washing, and boarding on heated forms.
Pairing, labels, header cards and cartons.

p: Report per pair by size and style, since an ankle sock and a knee-length sock carry very different yarn weights.

senseible: Senseible reads the plant's electricity bills (CEA grid factor 0.710 kg CO2 per kWh, CO2 Baseline Database version 21.0) and fuel invoices (IPCC 2006 defaults) into a fingerprinted Scope 1 and 2 record, the plant-level input to a per-unit figure. Bought-in materials go to the supplier evidence trail; product reports are self-declared drafts.
